_comment: The SHARED CONVERSION corpus (#6506). Read by BOTH scouts:
Third sibling of dedup_corpus.json (never file the same source twice) and
source_corpus.json (which lanes exist and what they admit). This one ties the
two implementations' answer to a different question: may the scout file AT ALL
today, given what happened to everything it already filed.
The observed defect: 160 filings, 117 still open AND still carrying
`needs-triage` (oldest 41.5 days), three more planned every morning, and every
run exiting 0 -- including the runs where all six Reddit queries returned HTTP
403. Discovery volume was measured; conversion never was. A gate that exists in
one implementation and not the other would be worthless here, because the
SCHEDULED daily path is tools/idea_scout.py while the interactive path is
`fak idea-scout` -- exactly the split that made #5543/#5544 the same defect
It lives under the Go package's testdata/ for the same reason its siblings do:
Go excludes testdata/ from builds and vet, while tools/*.json are scout CONFIG
files (--config) and a corpus dropped there would read as one.
_cap_comment: The declared ceiling on untriaged OPEN scout issues, in units of days-of-filing at max_issues=3: ~2 weeks of unattended filing may accumulate before the scout stops adding to it. Both implementations must default to this and both must expose it as the `untriaged_cap` threshold.
_status_comment: Precedence is degraded > paused > ok. A degraded run's candidate pool is incomplete, which invalidates every conclusion drawn from it -- including 'nothing new worth filing today' -- so it outranks the gate's own verdict, which stays separately readable in filing_gate.
_backlog_comment: Each case is a filed-issue corpus (the rung-2 shape gh returns for `issue list --label idea-scout --state all --json ...,state,stateReason,createdAt,labels`) and the ledger both implementations must fold it into. `filed -> triaged` is exact; `triaged -> shipped` is bounded, because GitHub reports COMPLETED both for a `Fixes #N` commit and for a hand closure, so `converted` is an UPPER bound on shipped effect.

backlog_cases.name: the-observed-audit-shape
backlog_cases.why: The #6506 shape in miniature: filings that were closed WITHOUT ever clearing needs-triage, mostly as not-planned. Counting a closure as triage would report a healthy loop; it must not.

backlog_cases.name: a-triaged-open-issue-is-not-untriaged
backlog_cases.why: The label coming off is the ONLY thing that moves an issue out of the untriaged stock, so the gate re-opens by itself as triage happens. An open issue a human already scoped counts as triaged and does not hold the gate.

backlog_cases.name: a-stateless-corpus-is-unclassified-not-empty
backlog_cases.why: A fixture replay (or a gh that stopped returning `state`) must read as a BLIND ledger, not as a backlog of zero. The count is what the fail-closed arm of the gate keys on.

backlog_cases.name: an-empty-history-converts-nothing-and-blocks-nothing
backlog_cases.why: The first-ever run. Rates are 0 by definition (no denominator), and nothing about that may read as a reason to pause.

_gate_comment: The gate takes the ledger above and the declared cap. Cases are stated on the ledger directly so both implementations answer the same question from the same numbers.

gate_cases.name: the-observed-stock-pauses-filing
gate_cases.why: THE #6506 CASE: 117 untriaged open against the default cap of 40. New filing stops until the stock drains.

gate_cases.name: a-drained-stock-re-opens-filing
gate_cases.why: Re-enablement is MECHANICAL, not a note in an issue: the same run that sees the stock back under the cap files again.

gate_cases.name: exactly-at-the-cap-still-files
gate_cases.why: The cap is the ceiling the stock may EXCEED before filing stops; at the cap the scout is still allowed its daily three.

gate_cases.name: a-negative-cap-disables-the-gate
gate_cases.why: The declared escape hatch, so a maintainer draining by hand can still gather and file without editing code.

gate_cases.name: a-zero-cap-pauses-on-any-untriaged-issue
gate_cases.why: 0 is the strictest posture: file only while nothing at all is waiting on triage.

gate_cases.name: a-blind-index-fails-closed
gate_cases.why: A corpus big enough to matter that reports NO state cannot be shown to be under the cap. 'We could not tell' must not read as 'we are fine' -- a census that fails open has no meaning.

gate_cases.name: a-small-blind-corpus-does-not-fail-closed
gate_cases.why: A fixture replay of a handful of issues is not evidence of an unmeasurable backlog; the fail-closed arm only engages once the blind corpus alone would exceed the cap.

_lane_comment: Source health: which lanes were ATTEMPTED (derived from the topics, so a lane that failed before reporting anything is still covered) against the `lane[topic]: …` errors the gatherer recorded. A lane that failed on every topic that armed it is `down`, and one down lane degrades the whole run.

lane_cases.name: reddit-403-on-every-topic-is-down-and-degrades-the-run
lane_cases.why: THE OBSERVED CASE: six Reddit queries, six HTTP 403s, run exits 0. It must now report status=degraded.

lane_cases.name: one-flaky-topic-is-partial-not-degraded
lane_cases.why: A single failed query is weather. Degrading on it would train the operator to ignore the status.

lane_cases.name: filing-errors-are-not-source-lanes
lane_cases.why: `create[github:o/r]: …` has the same lane[topic] SHAPE as a source error. Attributing it to a lane would invent a dead source out of a failed issue creation.

lane_cases.name: the-fresh-lane-is-only-attempted-when-it-is-armed
lane_cases.why: fresh_per_topic: 0 disables the lane. Counting it as attempted-and-healthy would report a lane the gatherer never walks.
